findings.title: Partial-month test does not exercise rounding
findings.explanation: 3000 cents over 30 days with a 10-day offset gives exactly 2000, so the test passes whether or not the implementation rounds correctly. Money values that don't divide evenly (for example 1000 cents, 7 days used of 30) are where proration bugs occur, such as fractional cents, floating-point drift, or a floor/round/ceil choice. Add a case with a non-divisible amount and assert the expected integer result, so the rounding rule is pinned down.

findings.title: Degenerate period (start equals end) is not covered
findings.explanation: The PR covers boundary cancellations, but not a zero-length period (start === end), where a naive implementation divides by zero and returns NaN. It also does not cover an inverted period (end before start). Add a test that documents the intended behavior (0, throw, or full amount) so a regression is caught.

findings.title: Missing sub-day and time-of-day cases
findings.explanation: All dates are exactly midnight UTC. Proration is usually computed in milliseconds or days, and the choice affects the result when cancellation happens mid-day (for example 2026-04-11T12:00:00Z). One test with a non-midnight timestamp would show whether partial days are counted. Month lengths of 28 and 31 days would also be worth covering, since only a 30-day period is tested.

findings.title: Duplicated start/end fixtures
findings.explanation: Every test redeclares the same start and end dates. Hoisting them into shared constants (or a beforeEach) would reduce noise and make the new cases easier to read. Alternatively, use it.each for the boundary cases.

## Add edge-case tests for proration

Covers cancellations at the start and end of a period, before it starts, after it ends, and a partial month.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/tests/billing.test.ts b/tests/billing.test.ts
index 0d7643a..81a4aa1 100644
--- a/tests/billing.test.ts
+++ b/tests/billing.test.ts
@@ -19,4 +19,24 @@ describe('proratedAmount', () => {
     const end = new Date('2026-05-01T00:00:00Z')
     expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, new Date('2026-04-16T00:00:00Z'))).toBe(1500)
   })
+
+  it('refunds everything when cancelled at or before the start', () => {
+    const start = new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00Z')
+    const end = new Date('2026-05-01T00:00:00Z')
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, start)).toBe(3000)
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, new Date('2026-03-20T00:00:00Z'))).toBe(3000)
+  })
+
+  it('refunds nothing when cancelled at or after the end', () => {
+    const start = new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00Z')
+    const end = new Date('2026-05-01T00:00:00Z')
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, end)).toBe(0)
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, new Date('2026-05-09T00:00:00Z'))).toBe(0)
+  })
+
+  it('refunds two thirds after ten days of a thirty-day period', () => {
+    const start = new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00Z')
+    const end = new Date('2026-05-01T00:00:00Z')
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, new Date('2026-04-11T00:00:00Z'))).toBe(2000)
+  })
 })
```
